content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes a unified parameter adapter tuning for the transformer based archtiectures in the domain of class incremental learning (CIL). It also mildly modifies the memory replaying to enhance the performance. 

The experiments are conducting on CIFAR-100, Standford-cars and Oxford-flowers.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
I unfortunately did not find a significant strength to discuss here. 

Weaknesses

The novelty and scope of this work is limited. For the novelty part, it simply combines two previous approaches, prompt token based and adapter based into a unified framework, and mildly modify the well-known memory replying technique. For the scope of this work, it only considers the transformer based archtiectures in their methodology, though ideally it might apply to other techniques. 

I have several questions throughout the reading

1. This method is a combination of previous methods, make the claim of this work weak. 
 
 In the introduction, the authors motivate their approach by criticizing the memory replaying approachs: "memory overhead required for replaying become unacceptable for practical applications". First, I am not sure why this is the case. Does it mean, if you treat the ImageNet 1000 classes as an incremental learning problem, the complexity of training all 1000 classes is O(n), replaying will be O(n^2) that might be unacceptable? 

If this is the case, then why the authors also propose a simple basic memory replaying to introduce this "unacceptable" complexity? This seeems to be contradictory.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The clarity of this work is not satisfactory. 

The organization of this work also seems pretty rough, hope the authors could carefully trim this paper before their resubmission.
content.summary_of_the_review: Due to the limited novelty, the poor quality of this work, I vote to reject this paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper conducts class incremental learning based on efficient tuning and pre-trained VIT, and makes use of memory replay to keep the previous knowledge. In order to save additional memory space, this paper proposes a method to synthesize images.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
  (1) The problem setting is interesting.
  (2) Incremental learning with a large pre-trained model is practical. 

Weaknesses: 
(1) L2P and DualPrompt work much worse than the results reported in the original papers. For example, the final acc of DualPrompt on cifar100 of 10 phases is 86.51, which is much higher than the result reported in this paper (76.78) and also higher than the highest result reported by the proposed method (80.06). Therefore, the state-of-the-art performance of this paper is overclaimed, and the results reported by this paper lack credibility. Since both of these two methods officially release their code, the author should conduct experiments the same as their setting and report comparable results to support your SOTA claim. (The third contribution can not stand.)
(2) The novelty of this paper is limited, combining prompt-tuning and adapter-tuning is trivial, and using knowledge distilling is also a common practice. (The first contribution is too trivial.) 
(3) Therefore, the only contribution is how to synthesize data to save replay memory. However, this is not a brand-new idea. Data-free distilling has already been applied to incremental learning [1]. What's more, the additional memory consumption compared with DualPrompt is missing. I can not find out the advantages when compared with DualPrompt. (Please refer to [2] Table 2)

[1] Always Be Dreaming: A New Approach for Data-Free Class-Incremental Learning.
[2] DualPrompt: Complementary Prompting for Rehearsal-free Continual Learning

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes UPAT: a combination of prompt-based and adapter-based tuning for class incremental learning. Meanwhile, to reduce forgetting, it introduces basic memory replay (BMR) with fixed memory usage. By linearly combining the basic samples, BMR can synthesize many visual inter-task samples. A feature distillation loss is also used to make the output representation from the new model consistent with the pre-trained model. Experiments show higher final accuracy but at a cost of higher average forgetting compared with only tuning prototypes (ITP).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
1. The method integrates prompt-tuning and adapter-tuning for class incremental learning.

2. The basic memory replay is proposed to reduce the memory footprint by synthesizing virtual with a linear combination of basic samples.

3. Experiments show it obtains higher final accuracy than other PAT-based methods.

Weaknesses
1. The problem definition lacks much context to understand the incremental learning. What’s the relation of X, D and X^y? The superscript of x/X keeps changing, which makes it difficult to understand their meanings. The X^{s_t+1} appears twice in D_t, which seems incorrect. It would be better to give a more detailed introduction of the incremental learning problem. 

2. Section 3.2 fails to play the role of preliminary. The concept of prototype is given here, but it is directly used here.  There is no intuition given behind tuning the example prototypes. A clear procedure of tuning also lacks. The k-means clustering and MSL comes out with little introduction. Some intuitive introductions are more helpful to the equations. The notations are kind of not straightforward to understand, e.g, y_k(e^j_i). I think it’s necessary to optimize the notations in equations.

3. Equation 1 comes out with lack of context. The description of “ N_e example e_i” is quite confusing. Why use uppercase N? Why does e appear in different positions in the two notations? The appearance of g(x) also gives surprise since it looks like a function, but actually refers to a class. 

4. Training has three stages, which is kind of not efficient.

5. The loss in Equation 14 has 4 hyperparameter lambdas. It’s unclear how to choose them and how sensitive they are.

5. The experiments only use one backbone: VitB/16 pre-trained on CLIP400M.

6. Some font sizes in Figure 2 are kind of too small to read.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The methods is combination of prompt-tuning and adaptor-tuning for ICL is kind of novel, but seems straightforward.

2. The paper organization and writing have much improvement space. Though Figure 1 gives a clear presentation of the UPAT architecture, Figure 2, Sections 3 and 4 don't introduce the method and losses well. After reading the paper, It's still unclear how the BMR is trained together with the k-means and the sample selection.

3. There are three stages in training and several hyper-parameters to tune. The reproducibility and generalization to other backbones (besides the VitB/16) are questionable.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper follows the parameters-additional-tuning to improve class incremental learning. The combination of adapter and prompt tuning is interesting, but the overall method including basic memory replay and feature distillation seem some over-complex. Moreover, the current paper presentation makes it kind of difficult to understand the method.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors try to improve parameter-additional-tuning (PAT) methods for class-incremental learning. First, they propose a unified PAT framework that transfers a fixed pre-trained vision transformer to sequential arrival downstream tasks. Second, they propose basic memory replaying that synthesizes on-call virtual old samples. Extensive experiment results on multiple datasets are provided.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strengths

- This paper is well-organized and easy to follow. 
- The proposed method is technically sound.
- Extensive experiment results are provided

### Weaknesses

- The technical novelty of the unified PAT is somewhat limited. It seems a combination of prompt-based and adapter-based methods. 

- It is not reasonable to use a VitB/16 model pre-trained on CLIP400M to run class-incremental learning experiments on CIFAR-100. Because the concepts have already been included in the pre-trained model. 

- Existing class-incremental learning papers usually run experiments on ImageNet-Subset and ImageNet-1k [A, B]. However, this paper only provides the results on Stanford-Cars and Oxford-Flower. It would be better to also provide results on ImageNet. 

- Existing class-incremental learning papers usually use ResNet-32 to run experiments on CIFAR-100. However, the authors use VitB/16 in this paper. Thus, it is important to provide a comparison of the memory usage and computational costs of the model between existing methods [A, B] and the proposed method.  

[A] Rebuffi, Sylvestre-Alvise, et al. "icarl: Incremental classifier and representation learning." Proceedings of the IEEE conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2017.
[B] Hou, Saihui, et al. "Learning a unified classifier incrementally via rebalancing." Proceedings of the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition. 2019.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
### Clarity & Quality

The paper is well-written and easy to follow. 

### Novelty 

The energy-based method for CIL seems interesting. However, we still need to validate that the proposed method doesn’t violate the memory usage protocol in CIL.

### Reproducibility

The authors didn’t provide the open-source code.

content.title: Incremental Unified Parameter Additional Tuning with Basic Memory Replaying
content.TL;DR: We propose a novel method for class incremental learning by tuning an unified additional parameter structure and replaying basic memory.
content.abstract: Class incremental learning (CIL) aims to develop an open intelligence system that can continuously learn new concepts from new tasks while retaining the knowledge to distinguish between new and old concepts. Recently, parameter-additional-tuning methods (PAT) have successfully alleviated catastrophic forgetting by starting from a well-pre-trained model and only allowing a few additional parameters to be trained. However, the contradiction between stability and plasticity and the lack of inter-task features still challenge PAT-based CIL methods. To address these, we propose Unified PAT and basic memory replaying (BMR). On the one hand, unified PAT transfer the model to sequential arrival downstream tasks based on a fixed pre-trained vision transformer by unifying the prompt-based and the adapter-based methods, offering more diversified plastic structures to efficiently capture more useful features without large-scale parameters. On the other hand, BMR synthesizes on-call virtual old samples with a fixed-size basic memory to create a global task that covers up all the sub-tasks, which makes inter-task features more learnable without a large memory budget. Abundant experiments prove the effectiveness of our method.
